newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPANISH MATCHES SCHEDULED FOR THE WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH MATCHES SCHEDULED FOR THE WEEKEND.

text.p: Spanish league championship matches scheduled for the weekend: (league standings in parentheses, kick-off times gmt)

Suspended defender Jose Prieto will be out for Sevilla who are desperate for points against a Valencia side that suffered a UEFA Cup setback midweek against Schalke 04, and where coach Jorge Valdano and the club board are under increasing pressure.

Sporting went down 4-2 to Betis in a midweek game, and will again be looking for breathing space against fellow strugglers Logrones, one of 11 teams with very real relegation problems. Logrones look set to reshape the left side of midfield.

Barcelona's Ronaldo was sensational in the 5-1 win at Compostela earlier this season, but Barcelona have blown a fuse since then and are now struggling to hang on to second. Keeper Vitor Baia and defender Fernando Couto will again be absent.

Croatian Alen Peternac and strike partner Jose Quevedo return for Valladolid against a Tenerife side that went down midweek in the UEFA Cup but will be looking to ensure a place in next season's competition.
Defender Loren Juarros has recovered from injury but Real defender Alberto Albistegui is still out with a nose injury. Playmaker Pedro Jose Lorenzo is out of the rapidly improving Extremadura outfit.

Celta are without still without injured striker Vlaadimir Gudelj, while coach Fernando Santos continues to monitor the recovery of defenders Patxi Salinas and Adriano. UEFA Cup side Espanyol have slipped to 20th and badly need the points.

Deportivo will be without defender Miroslav Djukic and midfielder Fran Gonzalez and will again look to Brazilian playmaker Rivaldo for inspiration against an Oviedo side that will be without injured Czech midfielder Peter Dubovsky.
Rayo were boosted by the 2-0 defeat of Sevilla midweek and will be hoping to move further out of the danger area against a side that look odds-on favourites to return to the second divsion.

Defender Hristo Vidakovic will again rested by Betis manager Lorenzo Serra Ferrer for this vital game between two sides eager to take Spain's second Champions' League place. Atletico may show the effects of midweek European action at Ajax.
Athletic golden boy Julen Guerrero will sit out the game with an ankle injury, while Gustavo Poyet's presence in an improving Zaragoza side depends on an appeal against suspension.

Real's second successive Monday game reflects their absence from European and domestic Cups. Real will be without striker Emilio Amavisca and will hope to stretch their nine-point lead against a side that has taken points from 11 of their 14 away games.
